clue.text: Hurry, if you want to use the weighing machine

definitions.meaning: a brusque order to go faster, as to a driver

definitions.text: if you want to use the weighing machine
definitions.meaning: taken literally, the phrase is an instruction to stand on the scales

explanation.surface: A joke notice by the bathroom scales telling someone to get a move on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges speed, from pressing the accelerator pedal hard; literally it means to climb onto something.

clue.text: Relationship between matron and nurse

definitions.meaning: a female sibling is a family relationship
in British hospitals this rank of nurse ranked above an ordinary nurse and below the matron

explanation.surface: A question about how two hospital staff get on at work.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a ward's senior nurse is traditionally called by this title, ranking between staff nurse and matron.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a kinship term and a nursing rank, so it fits both halves of the hospital picture.

clue.text: Pass in English, overlooking slight error

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a lapse is a minor slip or mistake

explanation.surface: An English exam passed despite a small mistake going unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or go by; the verb for time slipping away is a synonym.

clue.text: Not on time, when trade is slack

parts.note: something not on is off, as a cancelled event
a season is a period of time

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's remark that business arrives late during the quiet months.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet part of the year in tourism or retail, when fewer customers come, is this period.

clue.text: I shall receive therapy for abuse

indicators.note: the first person takes on the therapy, which follows it here

parts.note: contracted, I shall becomes I'll
therapy is medical treatment

explanation.surface: A patient saying they will get therapy to recover from abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel or harmful handling of someone is a synonym of abuse.

clue.text: High-rise central block

parts.note: not a tower block but a compact mountain mass, recalling the famous French upland of that name with Central

explanation.surface: A description of a tall building in the middle of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-rise' suggests flats, but the block is of mountains; the Massif Central is a large upland in south-central France.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists use the word for a compact group of mountains forming a single upland block.

clue.text: Stay clear when hungry prima donna turns up

indicators.note: taken here as letting the empty letter sit within the overturned singer
in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer
hungry means empty, and O is the empty circle, zero

explanation.surface: Advice to keep away from a temperamental opera star who arrives famished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses DIVA to AVID, and the O for empty goes into it. AVID itself means hungry, a tempting false path that leaves the O unexplained.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep away from something is to shun it, the plain synonym.

clue.text: Pay to take residence at university?

parts.note: to settle is to make one's home somewhere
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A question whether paying is the price of moving into student halls.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to pay what is owed, clearing a bill.

clue.text: They go from bank to bank to stay business

definitions.text: They go from bank to bank to stay business

parts.words: They go from bank to bank to stay business
parts.note: the banks are river banks, crossed back and forth by boatmen carrying passengers, not financial houses

explanation.surface: Traders shuttling between financial institutions to keep their firm afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests money banks; the banks are a river's sides and the business is carrying passengers across.
explanation.definitionFit: Boatmen who carry people across a river ply between its two banks for a living.

clue.text: It's put up for work on the outside

definitions.text: It's put up for work on the outside

parts.words: It's put up for work on the outside
parts.note: a temporary framework is erected so builders can reach a building's exterior; also hints at the gallows put up for an execution

explanation.surface: Something displayed for outside work, like a job notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders erect a temporary structure of poles and planks to work on a building's exterior walls.

clue.text: Who's this first on TV? No, in Bond film

definitions.text: Who's this first on TV? No, in Bond film

parts.words: Who's this first on TV? No, in Bond film
parts.note: the title comes before Who in the TV series and before No in the first James Bond film

explanation.surface: A quiz question about which actor appeared first, on television or in a spy film.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction series; Dr. No (1962) was the first James Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical title prefixes both the BBC time traveller's name and the Bond villain's.

clue.text: Turns up a real oddity — it's uncanny

indicators.note: an oddity is something strange, so the letters are made strange by being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that a genuine curiosity has appeared, which is eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond natural explanation is eerie or unearthly, a synonym of uncanny.

clue.text: Girl's back to oriental island

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from the end to the start

parts.note: E for east, the oriental direction
an isle is an island

explanation.surface: A young woman returning to an island in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's given name, an example of the class named.

clue.text: It's only a rude version of song and dance

indicators.note: a version is a reworked form, so the letters are given in a new order

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that a bawdy number is merely a crude rendering of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a short medieval song with a refrain, and also a circle dance accompanying it.

clue.text: The key part of a Houdini contract?

definitions.text: The key part of a Houdini contract?

parts.words: The key part of a Houdini contract?
parts.note: the famous escapologist's contract would naturally centre on the provision letting a party get out of it

explanation.surface: A question about the vital term in the great escapologist's agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Houdini was the celebrated escape artist, so the provision for getting out is aptly his key clause.
explanation.definitionFit: A provision allowing a party to withdraw from an agreement under stated conditions.

clue.text: Plan to surprise carol singer, after extra rest

indicators.note: the singer comes after the rest, so it is placed second

parts.note: a lie-in is an extra stay in bed in the morning
the waits were bands of carol singers going round at Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone planning to startle a carol singer once they have slept late.
explanation.walkthrough: Waits are a traditional British name for groups of Christmas carol singers.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide ready to ambush someone is to plan a surprise attack on them.

clue.text: It sounds highly unnatural

parts.note: a man's artificially high singing voice sounds unnaturally high-pitched

explanation.surface: A comment that something seems most implausible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' is a real verb about noise here, not a sign of a word said aloud, and 'highly' means at high pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer's voice forced above its natural range produces a high, unnatural tone.

clue.text: Refuse CO agitating to send in troops

indicators.note: agitating means stirring up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A commanding officer is pressed to deploy soldiers and declines.
explanation.walkthrough: CO is the usual abbreviation for commanding officer, but here it is simply two letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Deploying soldiers means resorting to military might, the phrase's sense.

clue.text: Far away — and not appearing to be distressed

parts.note: someone not appearing is absent
to have minded something is to have been upset by it

explanation.surface: A person who is distant and seems untroubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Far away describes a dreamy, preoccupied look, which is forgetful inattention.

clue.text: A way the head master initially receives a complaint

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letters of the words head and master are used

parts.note: the letters so far take in a single letter A at the end

explanation.surface: A headmaster on his rounds hears a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here is a medical sense, an ailment; this breathing disorder is one example.

clue.text: Place for a president to see twice

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
the word see is used a second time, now as itself

explanation.surface: A spot where a president might look on two occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see twice': one see is a bishop's see, Ely, and the second is just the word. Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: The French president's official residence in Paris is the Élysée Palace.

clue.text: A device for catching people in the act?

definitions.text: A device for catching people in the act?

parts.words: A device for catching people in the act?
parts.note: the act is a circus act, and acrobats who fall are caught by a mesh below

explanation.surface: A trap or camera for catching criminals red-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the act' suggests catching wrongdoers, but the act is a trapeze performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh stretched beneath trapeze artists catches them if they fall during a performance.

clue.text: Crown jewels?

parts.note: not the royal regalia but a jewelled headdress worn on top of the head, the crown

explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular headband sits on the crown of the head, so it is literally jewels for the crown.

clue.text: Alan's wrong to be nosy

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of order and must be put right

explanation.surface: Someone telling Alan that prying is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nosy' normally means prying, but here it means of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally, nosy means relating to the nose, which is what this adjective means.

clue.text: Sailor, a Scotsman, is seen on the roads

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Mac, from the Gaelic prefix of many surnames, is slang for a Scot

explanation.surface: A sailor and a Scot are spotted walking the highways.
explanation.definitionFit: The black surfacing material laid on streets is what one sees underfoot on a highway.

clue.text: Breaks in knee-length trousers, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the trousers word is said out loud

parts.note: breeches are trousers fastened just below the knee

explanation.surface: Tears appearing in someone's riding trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rupture or gap, as in a wall, or the breaking of a rule, is a synonym of breaks.

clue.text: A method for dealing with traffic?

definitions.text: A method for dealing with traffic?

parts.note: a, as a single one, gives ONE
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A question about how to manage congestion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a single-direction scheme is one way of handling vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A street restricted to vehicles travelling in a single direction is a common traffic scheme.

clue.text: Stout friend, about 50, who shares digs

indicators.note: the word for stout goes about, around, the numeral

parts.note: a stout person is fat
L is the Roman numeral for 50
mate is informal for friend

explanation.surface: A portly pal of about fifty who lives in the same lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' does not mean roughly here; it puts L inside FAT. Digs is British slang for lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharing a rented apartment is a co-tenant, the person who shares lodgings.
